note: Rewritten from Sands' (1999) new species description, original in English; the genus lacks soldiers, only the worker has a complete description; measurements follow the original ranges (the original does not list the fore tibia length).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: From A. camerunensis it differs in having shorter legs, the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible as long as that of the first, the proximal end of the fourth marginal tooth not touching the molar prominence, the third lobe of the enteric valve seat nearly as large as the other two lobes, and the spines of the primary rows curved on the three-radiate valve. From A. cristatus it differs in that the latter is larger, has longer fore legs, the fourth marginal tooth of the left mandible just touching the lateral edge of the molar prominence, and large, straight primary-row spines on a nearly six-radiate valve. From A. dibogi it differs in that the latter has the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible shorter than that of the first marginal tooth, the fourth marginal tooth just touching the lateral edge of the molar prominence, a long and inflated first hindgut segment, the enteric valve seat situated dorsolaterally on the left, and a six-radiate enteric valve with fine straight spines and spinose scales, unique in the genus. From A. ivorensis it differs in that the latter has no conspicuous stout setae on the fore coxa.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white or pale yellow, the darkest part of the antennal flagellum pale yellow or yellow, pronotum and legs yellowish white, abdominal tergites transparent. Head capsule short-oval, nearly circular, setae sparse, or numerous but not dense, projecting, the longest setae arranged regularly and symmetrically. Fontanelle present as a pale spot or shallow depression, or absent. Anterior surface of the fore coxa with 4 or more stout setae arranged in rows or groups; fore tibia with 3 distal spurs, the third reduced or far smaller than the other two. Left mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth distinctly longer than the posterior margin or nearly equilateral, anterior margin of the third marginal tooth as long as that of the first marginal tooth, the proximal end of the fourth marginal tooth not touching the molar prominence in frontal view; right mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth shorter than that of the second marginal tooth. Measurements: head width 0.659—0.705 mm; pronotum width 0.410—0.472 mm, length 0.184—0.236 mm; hind tibia length 0.670—0.710 mm; left mandible index 0.808—1.205, right mandible index 0.971—1.374.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The midgut–hindgut junction arises ventrally to the left of the nerve cord or below it; the first hindgut segment is rather short, up to 8 times as long as its proximal width, tubular throughout; in the undissected abdomen the enteric valve lies to the right of the heart (dorsal view) or to the left of the nerve cord (ventral view); the third lobe of the enteric valve seat is nearly as large as the outer pair. The enteric valve ridges are nearly taper-ellipsoid from the base towards the apical spines, or are markedly waisted at the base of the apical spines and then widen, the ends weakly sclerotized, pale yellow or yellow; the primary rows bear very long tapering spines, ridges one and three with at most 10—14, ridges two and four with at most 10, the longest curved but evenly tapering, not wider than the narrowest point of ridge three, the symmetry nearly three-radiate, the intercalary ridges reduced; the secondary rows bear sparser conspicuous spines, lengthening towards the ridge apex, the scales or reticulation distinct; the membrane between and outside the ridges bears numerous but not dense minute spines, with marginal scales proximally.
